hunks.baseline: With a grisly sound, white teeth shot into the air.
hunks.sol: With a grisly crunch, white teeth shot into the air.

hunks.baseline: They had been maintained so meticulously that they gleamed even in the darkness. It had all become pointless now, though.
hunks.sol: He had taken such meticulous care of them that they gleamed even in the darkness. Not that it mattered anymore.

hunks.baseline: Won Myunghoon flew several meters before slamming his back into a tree and coughing.
hunks.sol: Won Myunghoon flew several meters before slamming back-first into a tree and coughing violently.

hunks.baseline: The teeth that had remained in his mouth fell out in little clumps, mixed with blood. When he finally raised his head, his face was twisted in shock.
hunks.sol: The teeth left in his mouth tumbled out with the blood. When he finally raised his head, his face was twisted in shock.

hunks.baseline: It had happened in the blink of an eye.
hunks.sol: It had all happened in the blink of an eye.

hunks.baseline: And it wasn’t only Won Myunghoon. Every Star Guild member stared at me with an expression of disbelief.
hunks.sol: And it wasn’t only Won Myunghoon. Every Star Guild member stared at me in disbelief.

hunks.baseline: “How? Because I’m stronger than you.”
hunks.sol: “What do you mean, how? I’m stronger than you. That’s how.”

hunks.baseline: At my breezy answer and the single step I took forward, Won Myunghoon’s body began to tremble.
hunks.sol: I gave him a breezy answer and took a single step forward. Won Myunghoon began to tremble.

hunks.baseline: “Did I come here? You’re the ones who were waiting for me.”
hunks.sol: “Did I come looking for you? You’re the ones who were waiting for me.”

hunks.baseline: Perhaps sensing the danger, Won Myunghoon shouted as if throwing a fit.
hunks.sol: Perhaps sensing the danger, Won Myunghoon shrieked as if having a fit.

hunks.baseline: “There are only two of them! If we back down here, every last one of us is going to die!”
hunks.sol: “There are only two of them! If we back down now, every last one of us is going to die!”

hunks.baseline: The Star Guild members had hesitated, but at his command, they raised their weapons. Won Myunghoon gritted his teeth around the few that remained.
hunks.sol: The hesitant Star Guild members raised their weapons at his command. Won Myunghoon gritted the few teeth he had left.

hunks.baseline: I stopped walking.
hunks.sol: I stopped.

hunks.baseline: Won Myunghoon snorted and glared at me with burning eyes.
hunks.sol: Won Myunghoon snorted and glared at me with blazing eyes.

hunks.baseline: “Don’t pretend you don’t know. You obviously found some high-performance acceleration Equipment somewhere and put it on…”
hunks.sol: “Don’t play dumb. You obviously found some high-performance acceleration Equipment somewhere and put it on…”

hunks.baseline: “Oh, that’s what you mean?”
hunks.sol: “Oh, that’s what you meant?”

hunks.baseline: I widened my eyes in surprise.
hunks.sol: My eyes widened in surprise.

hunks.baseline: Won Myunghoon’s imagination was astonishing. He was somehow rationalizing the reason he had lost.
hunks.sol: Won Myunghoon’s imagination was impressive. He had somehow managed to rationalize his defeat.

hunks.baseline: “That’s a pretty original idea. But compared to that, isn’t this hostage situation a little too cliché?”
hunks.sol: “That’s a pretty original theory. But isn’t the hostage routine a little cliché by comparison?”

hunks.baseline: “Cliché or not, the important thing is that it always works.”
hunks.sol: “It may be cliché, but the important thing is that it always works.”

hunks.baseline: “Maybe…”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know about that…”

hunks.baseline: While I exchanged those few words with Won Myunghoon, the Star Guild members charged toward Butler Kim with their tanks at the front.
hunks.sol: While Won Myunghoon and I exchanged those few words, the Star Guild members charged toward Butler Kim with their tanks leading the way.

hunks.baseline: The moment Won Myunghoon questioned me, Butler Kim—who had been massaging his lower back—drove his long staff into the ground.
hunks.sol: The moment Won Myunghoon questioned me, Butler Kim—who had been massaging his lower back—planted his long staff against the ground.

hunks.baseline: It was a light movement. Yet the power that flowed from the end of his staff shook the earth.
hunks.sol: It was a light movement. Yet the power flowing from the tip of his staff shook the earth.

hunks.baseline: The primeval forest trembled violently.
hunks.sol: The primeval forest convulsed.

hunks.baseline: Cracks split the solid ground. Dirt and rocks shot into the air, exposing the trunks of trees that had sunk their roots deep into the earth. Flocks of nameless birds took flight.
hunks.sol: Cracks split the solid ground. Dirt and rocks erupted into the air, exposing the roots of deeply rooted trees. Flocks of nameless birds took flight.

hunks.baseline: Unfortunately for the Star Guild members, they had no wings. The cracked and shattered ground surged up like triangular waves and swallowed them whole.
hunks.sol: Unfortunately for the Star Guild members, they had no wings. The cracked and shattered ground surged like jagged waves and swallowed them whole.

hunks.baseline: “Everyone, get out of the way—urk!”
hunks.sol: “Everyone, get out of the—urk!”

hunks.baseline: After the waves swept through, only groans and screams drifted sporadically through the forest.
hunks.sol: Once the waves had swept past, only scattered groans and screams drifted through the forest.

hunks.baseline: The Star Guild members were crushed beneath an enormous weight of earth and rubble, barely able to keep their heads above the surface as they gasped for breath.
hunks.sol: The Star Guild members lay crushed beneath an enormous weight of earth and rubble, barely managing to keep their heads exposed as they gasped for breath.

hunks.baseline: The man who had rendered around a dozen veteran B-Rank Hunters incapable of fighting with a single spell could not have looked more at ease.
hunks.sol: The man who had incapacitated around a dozen veteran B-Rank Hunters with a single spell could not have looked more at ease.

hunks.baseline: “Young friends, you have no manners toward your Senior. Relax and close your eyes, all of you. Unless you want to be buried alive.”
hunks.sol: “Young men these days have no respect for their Senior. Stop struggling and close your eyes, all of you—unless you want to be buried alive.”

hunks.baseline: It was a chilling voice, unlike anything I had heard from him before.
hunks.sol: His voice was chilling, unlike anything I had ever heard from him before.

hunks.baseline: Only then did the Star Guild members realize Butler Kim’s true abilities. Their faces went pale as they lowered their heads.
hunks.sol: Only then did the Star Guild members realize the true extent of Butler Kim’s abilities. Their faces went pale, and they lowered their heads.

hunks.baseline: A-Rank Hunters were rare, but A-Rank mages and healers were rarer still. The Star Guild members had probably never expected Butler Kim—who always kept his hands folded behind his back and laughed amiably—to be an A-Rank mage.
hunks.sol: A-Rank Hunters were rare, but mages and healers were rarer still among them. They probably never imagined that Butler Kim—the amiable old man who always stood with his hands behind his back—was an A-Rank mage.

hunks.baseline: I grinned at Won Myunghoon, whose body was trembling.
hunks.sol: I grinned at the trembling Won Myunghoon.

hunks.baseline: Won Myunghoon had been standing there blankly, like a man whose soul had left his body. At last, he managed to open his mouth.
hunks.sol: Won Myunghoon had been standing there blankly, as if his soul had left his body. At last, he managed to speak.

hunks.baseline: “You already know. The Peace Guild. We want to live up to our name, but the people around us won’t cooperate.”
hunks.sol: “You already know. We’re the Peace Guild. We’d like to live up to our name, but no one around us seems willing to cooperate.”

hunks.baseline: He could never have imagined that one wrong choice would lead to a result like this.
hunks.sol: He could never have imagined that one bad decision would lead to this.

hunks.baseline: But it was already too late to turn back. A hyena cornered at the edge of a cliff had only two options left.
hunks.sol: But it was already too late to turn back. A cornered hyena had only two choices left.

hunks.baseline: I walked toward Won Myunghoon. After kicking the fallen spear far away, I watched as he lowered his head in resignation.
hunks.sol: I walked toward him. When I kicked the fallen spear far away, he lowered his head in resignation.

hunks.baseline: “This suddenly?”
hunks.sol: “Just like that?”

hunks.baseline: Even though I was standing right in front of him, he did not move. I asked the man who refused to answer with his head bowed.
hunks.sol: Even with me standing right in front of him, he didn’t move. I addressed him as he stood there silently with his head bowed.

hunks.baseline: “Once you get out, you’re looking at life imprisonment at minimum. You know how serious a crime what you did in a Gate is, don’t you?”
hunks.sol: “Once we get out, you’re looking at life in prison at the very least. You know how serious a crime this is inside a Gate, don’t you?”

hunks.baseline: After hesitating, Won Myunghoon spoke.
hunks.sol: After a moment’s hesitation, Won Myunghoon spoke.

hunks.baseline: “Because it’s better than dying.”
hunks.sol: “It’s better than dying.”

hunks.baseline: If he survived, there would still be a chance. Death, on the other hand, was absolute. Whatever lay beyond it was something he would find out afterward.
hunks.sol: As long as he survived, there would still be a chance. Death, on the other hand, meant a complete end. Whatever lay beyond it was something he would only discover afterward.

hunks.baseline: People with a lot to lose were afraid of death. Won Myunghoon was one of them.
hunks.sol: People with a lot to lose tended to fear death. Won Myunghoon was no exception.

hunks.baseline: In those twin pupils, dark as an abyss, some unknowable light swirled.
hunks.sol: An unknowable light swirled within those twin pupils, dark as the abyss.

hunks.baseline: Fear of the future that awaited him. Anxiety over death.
hunks.sol: Fear of the future awaiting him. Anxiety over death.

hunks.baseline: And then…
hunks.sol: And…

hunks.baseline: “Just once. Give me one last chance. Killing a man like me will only leave you with a bad taste in your mouth.”
hunks.sol: “Just once. Give me one last chance. Killing someone like me will only leave a bad taste in your mouth.”

hunks.baseline: “It’ll leave a bad taste, but you won’t be punished. If you’re threatened with murder in a Gate, self-defense is recognized. You know that too.”
hunks.sol: “It might leave a bad taste, but I won’t be punished for it. Self-defense applies when someone threatens to kill you inside a Gate. You know that as well as I do.”

hunks.baseline: “If you kill me, it’s murder. The fact that you’ll become a murderer won’t change.”
hunks.sol: “If you kill me, it’s murder. That doesn’t change the fact that you’ll become a murderer.”

hunks.baseline: Murderer.
hunks.sol: *Murderer.*

hunks.baseline: The word rolling around on the tip of my tongue left a foul taste.
hunks.sol: The word tasted bitter on my tongue.

hunks.baseline: I looked down at Won Myunghoon, who was kneeling and begging for his life in a servile voice, then opened my mouth.
hunks.sol: I looked down at Won Myunghoon, kneeling before me and begging for his life in a servile voice, then spoke.

hunks.baseline: “One favor. Don’t betray my trust.”
hunks.sol: “But do me a favor. Don’t betray that trust.”

hunks.baseline: I tossed him a rope with instructions to bind himself, then turned around.
hunks.sol: I tossed him a rope and told him to bind himself. The moment I turned away—

hunks.baseline: That was when—
A shout filled with joy rang out, followed by killing intent from behind me.
hunks.sol: A triumphant shout rang out, and killing intent flared behind me.

hunks.baseline: I turned my head and saw Won Myunghoon charging right up to me. Somehow, he was holding a dagger infused with Aura.
hunks.sol: I turned my head. Won Myunghoon was already right on top of me, an Aura-infused dagger clutched in his hand.

hunks.baseline: Blood sprayed into the air with a short rush of displaced air. The joy that had brightly lit Won Myunghoon’s face gave way to puzzlement.
hunks.sol: A brief rush of displaced air—and a fountain of blood sprayed upward. The triumphant joy lighting Won Myunghoon’s face gave way to bewilderment.

hunks.baseline: It was a wrist, severed cleanly at the joint, still clutching the dagger whose Aura had vanished.
hunks.sol: It was Won Myunghoon’s wrist, cleanly severed and still clutching the dagger whose Aura had vanished.

hunks.baseline: “That should’ve been twice as fast.”
hunks.sol: “You needed to be at least twice that fast.”

hunks.baseline: I shook the blood from the dagger in my hand. In that brief instant, I had drawn a weapon from my Inventory, and the fight had ended in a heartbeat.
hunks.sol: I flicked the blood from the dagger in my hand. In that split second, I had drawn a weapon from my Inventory, and the fight had ended just as quickly.

hunks.baseline: A short silence—but one that felt like an eternity.
hunks.sol: A brief silence followed, though it felt like an eternity.

hunks.baseline: Then Won Myunghoon’s mouth slowly fell open, and a horrific scream burst forth.
hunks.sol: Then Won Myunghoon’s mouth slowly fell open, and a horrific scream burst from it.

hunks.baseline: As I watched him writhe in agony, my heart remained as calm and peaceful as a lake.
hunks.sol: As I watched him writhe in agony, my heart remained as still and peaceful as a lake.

hunks.baseline: I felt no sense of betrayal at having trusted someone who should never have been trusted. Not even the slightest regret.
hunks.sol: I felt no betrayal at having trusted someone I should never have trusted. Not even the slightest regret.

hunks.baseline: “Thanks. For doing exactly what I believed you would.”
hunks.sol: “Thanks. You did exactly what I trusted you to do.”

hunks.baseline: Not since the moment I received Yeti’s Necklace. Not since the moment he ignored my warning and bared his teeth at me again.
hunks.sol: Not since I received Yeti’s Necklace. Not since the moment he ignored my warning and bared his teeth at me again.

hunks.baseline: “You were exactly that kind of person.”
hunks.sol: “You were always exactly this kind of man.”

hunks.baseline: “If I leave you alive, you’ll bare your teeth at me again someday. Like a thorn lodged in the throat, you’ll find some way to come back if you survive.”
hunks.sol: “If I leave you alive, you’ll bare your teeth at me again someday. Like a thorn stuck in my throat, you’ll find some way to come back as long as you survive.”

hunks.baseline: My dagger severed the tendons in his calf. Blood spattered, and his knee buckled. Just as I pressed the razor-sharp blade against his neck—
hunks.sol: My dagger severed the tendons in his calf. Blood spattered, and his knee buckled. Just as I pressed the razor-sharp blade against his throat—

hunks.baseline: Several dozen meters away, Butler Kim was watching me with a look of concern.
hunks.sol: Several dozen meters away, Butler Kim was watching me with concern in his eyes.

hunks.baseline: “That’s right. That’s why I let him go once.”
hunks.sol: “You’re right. That’s why I let him go once.”

hunks.baseline: “But killing a monster and murdering someone are different. I’d rather do it myself—”
hunks.sol: “But killing a monster and murdering a person are different. I would rather do it myself—”

hunks.baseline: I replied in a calm voice.
hunks.sol: I answered calmly.

hunks.baseline: “I already know that very well.”
hunks.sol: “I know that perfectly well.”

hunks.baseline: How many people had I killed by now? Dozens? No, a hundred?
hunks.sol: How many people had I killed by now? Dozens? Maybe a hundred?

hunks.baseline: The world I had lived in had never been forgiving. In Gates, I had to kill monsters. In the Murim, I had to kill people.
hunks.sol: The worlds I had lived in had never been forgiving. Inside Gates, I had to kill monsters. In Murim, I had to kill people.

hunks.baseline: I was no lofty junzi. I was a Hunter and a martial artist with a family and people I had to protect. If it was necessary to survive or become stronger, I was willing to get blood on my hands.
hunks.sol: I was no lofty junzi. I was a Hunter and a martial artist with a family and people I had to protect. If surviving and becoming stronger meant getting blood on my hands, I would do it willingly.

hunks.baseline: To me, there was no great difference between a monster and Won Myunghoon before me.
hunks.sol: To me, there was little difference between a monster and Won Myunghoon.

hunks.baseline: *Because he’s an enemy.*
hunks.sol: *He was an enemy.*

hunks.baseline: Whoever that enemy was, if they were capable of harming me or my people someday, the right thing to do was to eliminate the source of the trouble.
hunks.sol: Whoever the enemy might be, if they could someday bring harm to me or my people, the right thing to do was eliminate the threat at its source.

hunks.baseline: Butler Kim had also fought his way through countless battlefields.
hunks.sol: Butler Kim had fought his way through countless battlefields himself.

hunks.baseline: He must have understood from that brief conversation alone. What kind of person I was, and what decision I had made.
hunks.sol: That brief exchange must have been enough for him to understand what kind of person I was—and what I had decided to do.

hunks.baseline: “Urgh. P-Please, spare me…”
hunks.sol: “Urgh. P-Please…spare me…”

hunks.baseline: I looked down at Won Myunghoon as he groaned.
hunks.sol: I looked down at the groaning Won Myunghoon.

hunks.baseline: He had once been the idol I looked up to as a child—the man who shone brighter than anyone among countless stars.
hunks.sol: He had once been the idol I looked up to as a child, a man who had shone brighter than any of the countless stars around him.

hunks.baseline: But I would put those old memories of him in a time capsule and bury them deep underground.
hunks.sol: But now I would seal those old memories inside a time capsule and bury them deep underground.

hunks.baseline: I whispered in a quiet voice.
hunks.sol: I whispered quietly.

hunks.baseline: “If you were going to try to kill someone, you should’ve been prepared to die, too.”
hunks.sol: “If you were going to kill someone, you should’ve been prepared to die.”

hunks.baseline: The dagger cut deep through his throat. Won Myunghoon’s eyes bulged as he looked up at me with a desperate gaze.
hunks.sol: The dagger cut deep into his throat. Won Myunghoon’s eyes bulged as he stared up at me pleadingly.

hunks.baseline: He tried to cover his throat with his one remaining hand, but he could not stop the blood—or his life—from pouring out.
hunks.sol: He tried to cover the wound with his one remaining hand, but he could stop neither the blood nor his life from pouring out.

hunks.baseline: Butler Kim nodded as he watched me with a strange look in his eyes.
hunks.sol: Butler Kim nodded, regarding me with an unreadable look.

hunks.baseline: He waved his staff, and the Star Guild members buried in the earth floated gently into the air.
hunks.sol: He waved his staff, and the Star Guild members buried beneath the earth floated gently into the air.

hunks.baseline: As I watched magical ropes being summoned and binding them tightly together like strings of dried fish, I suddenly spoke.
hunks.sol: As I watched conjured ropes bind them tightly together like strings of dried fish, something occurred to me.

hunks.baseline: A short while later, I followed the direction indicated by my Qi Sense and found a man with a gag in his mouth.
hunks.sol: A short while later, I followed my Qi Sense and found a gagged man.

hunks.baseline: For some reason, he was bound tightly to a tree. And he was someone I knew.
hunks.sol: For some reason, he had been bound tightly to a tree. And I recognized his face.

hunks.baseline: Most of the reporters who had flocked to cover the joint raid by the Peace Guild and the Star Guild—or rather, Jin Taekyung and Won Myunghoon’s raid—had left long ago.
hunks.sol: Most of the reporters who had flocked there to cover the joint raid between the Peace Guild and the Star Guild—or rather, the raid led by Jin Taekyung and Won Myunghoon—had left long ago.

hunks.baseline: But there were always exceptions. A young man wearing thick, horn-rimmed glasses and eating ramen was one of them.
hunks.sol: But there were always exceptions. One was a young man in thick, horn-rimmed glasses, eating ramen.

hunks.baseline: “Being the youngest is so miserable. So miserable.”
hunks.sol: “Being the youngest is miserable. Just miserable.”

hunks.baseline: At the young man’s lament, his colleague snickered as he picked up some instant kimchi.
hunks.sol: His colleague snickered and picked up a piece of instant kimchi.

hunks.baseline: “You’ve only been here two months, and you already have plenty to say.”
hunks.sol: “You’ve only been here two months, and you’re already full of complaints.”

hunks.baseline: “Come on. You haven’t been here that long either, Senior.”
hunks.sol: “Come on, Senior. You haven’t been here that long either.”

hunks.baseline: “Hey. Back in my day, I kept my mouth shut and worked. If they told me to stay, I stayed. If they told me to do something, I did it.”
hunks.sol: “Hey. Back in my day, I kept my mouth shut and did what I was told. If they told me to stay, I stayed. If they told me to tear someone apart in print, I did it.”

hunks.baseline: The young man stared glumly at the cup ramen, its surface shimmering with floating oil.
hunks.sol: The young man stared glumly into his cup ramen, where beads of oil floated across the surface.

hunks.baseline: “Three days? We should be grateful if they don’t stay the whole week.”
hunks.sol: “Three days? We should count ourselves lucky if they don’t stay the whole week.”

hunks.baseline: Seeing the other junior reporters in the same situation gathered around him and eating their meals only made him feel more depressed.
hunks.sol: Seeing groups of other junior reporters in the same miserable situation eating nearby only made him feel worse.

hunks.baseline: “They definitely won’t be out today. Like you said, even if they come out quickly, it’ll take three days. Get some sleep. Want to go to a sauna together? Maybe play some billiards?”
hunks.sol: “They definitely won’t be out today. Like you said, even if they’re quick, it’ll still take three days. Get some sleep. Want to hit a sauna together? Maybe play some billiards?”

hunks.sol: “Then maybe one game…”

hunks.sol: Tempted by his Senior’s offer, the young reporter had just begun to rise when—

hunks.sol: The enormous door looming before them—the Gate—gave off a strange sound.

hunks.baseline: “The cameras! Get them over here, quickly!”
hunks.sol: “The cameras! Get them over here, now!”

hunks.sol: The area descended into chaos. The reporters who had been idly passing the time shot to their feet and crowded in front of the Gate.

hunks.baseline: The young reporter and his Senior were no exception. They claimed a spot at the front faster than anyone else, their minds reeling.
hunks.sol: The young reporter and his Senior were no exception. They secured a place at the front faster than anyone else and frantically began preparing.

hunks.baseline: “What’s happening? Why are they coming out already?”
hunks.sol: “What’s going on? Why are they coming out already?”

hunks.baseline: The reporters had sensed that something had happened, and their prediction proved exactly right.
hunks.sol: The reporters sensed that something had happened, and their instincts proved exactly right.

hunks.baseline: Everyone who saw them stood with their mouths hanging open.
hunks.sol: Everyone who saw them stared with their mouths hanging open.
